stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = 2\left|x + 3\right| - 5\). The graph of \(y = f(x)\) in the \(xy\)-plane has two \(x\)-intercepts. What is the sum of the \(x\)-coordinates of the \(x\)-intercepts?
solution: The sum is \(-0.5 + (-5.5) = -6\). (The two intercepts are symmetric about the vertex at \(x = -3\), so the sum is \(2(-3)\).)

explanation.A: Incorrect. Both intercepts are negative, since the vertex is at \(x = -3\). The sum must be negative.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex of the graph, not the sum of the two \(x\)-intercepts.
explanation.C: Correct. The intercepts are at \(x = -0.5\) and \(x = -5.5\), whose sum is \(-6\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is one of the two intercepts, found from \(x + 3 = 2.5\). The case \(x + 3 = -2.5\) gives the other, \(x = -5.5\).

verify:
x = symbols('x', real=True)
roots = solve(Eq(2*Abs(x + 3) - 5, 0), x)
assert sorted(roots) == [Rational(-11, 2), Rational(-1, 2)]
assert value(choices[answer]) == sum(roots) == -6
assert all(value(choices[k]) != -6 for k in choices if k != answer)
